title: Serving Runtime Concierge — Weekly Ops Notes (Sep 15 2026)
content:
Purpose: weekly concierge-style operations notes for serving runtime (kernel, KV cache, batching). This doc is intended for quick handoffs to oncall and the kernel owners. Informal / operational - contains action items and a few live todos.

Summary highlights:
- Small kernel regression observed on Sept 13 during synthetic burst: p95 token latency rose ~18% for short-context requests (seq_len <= 128) when micro-batching enabled. Root cause sketch below.
- KV cache shadowing experiment continues: global prefill hit rate up to 27% (from 19%), but memory churn increased on instances with mixed-chat loads. Need eviction tuning.
- Concierge routing introduced for two noisy routes (customer A/B) reduced tail retries by ~40% by steering heavy tails to dedicated micro-pools.

Day-by-day notes (Sep 8 - Sep 15):
2026-09-08 (Tue) - Weekly kickoff
- Quick sync with kernel team. Patch set 1723 landed (PR link above) introducing speculative micro-batch fast-path. Initial perf good on bench.
- Action: Marco to add more safety checks for kv cache pointer validity (INF-2143).

2026-09-10 (Thu) - Observability check
- Noted small uptick in prefill eviction counts on staging for mixed-batch workloads. Prefill shadowing flagged higher memory pressure on 80GB nodes when concurrency > 64.
- Quick mitigation: lowered per-instance prefill retention window from 6m to 3m in canary. Metrics: prefill-hit rate dipped 1.5pp but memory churn reduced ~22%.

2026-09-13 (Sun) - Incident window (low-traffic weekend run)
- During a scheduled load test for new micro-batch fast-path, p95 token latency for seq_len <= 128 increased from 78ms to 92ms (median stable at ~25ms). No customer impact reported (weekend), flagged by oncall.
- Triage: kernel fast-path introduced a lock contention in cache lookup when batch coalescer triggered cancellation and re-queue (race with eviction sweep).
- Mitigation applied: temporarily disabled speculative fast-path on prod autoscaling group cs-prod-3.
- Rollback validated: p95 returned to baseline within 8 minutes.
- Action: Rina to reproduce failure with microbench harness and add invariant test for concurrent eviction+coalescer flows.

2026-09-14 (Mon) - Followups and experiments
- Rina reproduced scenario in local harness with 4000 small requests/s, confirmed contention under high eviction churn. Patch queued to add per-shard eviction mutex and lightweight CAS for coalescer tombstones.
- KV cache team trialed per-route cache weight allocation to protect small-context conversational customers from aggressive eviction. Early telemetry looks promising (less than 5% change in overall hit-rate for other tenants).

2026-09-15 (Tue) - Concierge routing and canary notes
- Concierge routing: we diverted two noisy customer routes (heavy bursty latency) to dedicated micro-pools with slightly looser batching windows. Outcome: retries and fallback invocations dropped ~40%, average per-request compute cost rose by ~6% but customer latency improved consistently.
- Canaries: deployed per-shard eviction mutex to 10% canary. No regressions after 24h. Next step to expand to 30% if no further issues.

Key metrics snapshot (canary vs baseline, aggregated):
- prefill hit rate: 27% (canary) vs 19% (baseline)
- p95 token latency (short ctx): 92ms (during regression) -> baseline 78ms -> canary with mutex 79ms
- memory churn (evictions/min per instance): down 22% after retention window tweak
- tail retries for noisy routes: down 40% after concierge routing

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Rina Chen: Add concurrent eviction+coalescer invariant tests and land kernel patch that uses per-shard eviction mutex. ETA: 2026-09-20.
- Marco Alvarez: Update INF-2143 doc with reproducer steps and link to PR; coordinate extended canary expansion. ETA: 2026-09-17.
- Aisha Patel (me): Draft 'concierge playbook' runbook for routing noisy routes, include SLO thresholds and cost tradeoffs. ETA: 2026-09-22.
- Liam O'Connor: Run a head-to-head of per-route cache weight allocation vs global LRU with sample customer traces. Deliver TL;DR and dataset by 2026-09-24.
- SRE: Add alert for eviction-spike (evictions/min per instance > 200) and a synthetic p95 check for short-seq requests in canaries. ETA: 2026-09-18.

Open questions / risks:
- How much buffer do we want in concierge routing before we mark a route as 'noisy'? Suggested thresholds: sustained 5x above baseline p95 OR >0.5% retry rate for 15m window. Need ops signoff.
- Prefill retention window tradeoffs: shorter window reduced memory churn but modestly lowered hit-rate. Do we prefer memory stability over slightly higher per-token cost? Ops input needed for large tenants.
- Kernel complexity growth: per-shard eviction mutex mitigates the immediate race but could add backpressure under extreme concurrency. We need load tests at 10k qps per-instance to validate.

Notes for oncall (quick checklist):
- If you see p95 spike on short-ctx and prefill-hit rate drop simultaneously: check canary -> if canary shows mutex non-degrading, consider expanding and routing noisy route to concierge pool.
- If memory churn high and eviction spikes: temporarily reduce prefill retention window on affected autoscaling group.
- If batching coalescer thrashes (lots of cancelled micro-batches): consider toggling coalescer allow-cancel flag to false for the pool and notify kernel owners.

Things to surface to product / solutions engineering:
- Concierge routing improved customer experience for two pilot customers but increased compute cost slightly. Suggest testing with 2 more pilot customers (GTM+pricing signoff required).
- Per-route cache weight allocation could become a product knob to offer 'conversation-friendly' tiers. Draft proposal in product backlog.

Appendix - Reproducer steps (short):
1) Run micro-bench harness (repo: serving-runtime/tests/microbench) with 4000 rps, seq_len distribution: 80% <= 128, 20% 512.
2) Enable speculative micro-batch fast-path and prefill retention window = 6m.
3) Add background eviction sweep noise (script included in harness) to simulate mixed-tenant memory pressure.
4) Observe p95 and thread contention metrics on kernel threadpool.

Next week plan:
- Land Rina's kernel patch and expand canary to 30% if green.
- Complete concierge playbook and get ops signoff on routing thresholds.
- Run 10k qps per-instance load test to validate mutex behavior.
- Product: sync on per-route cache weight proposal and pricing implications.

Notes-to-self: capture a short runbook section for support tier 2 -> how to toggle concierge routing, how to read prefill hit-rate dashboards, and where to find microbench reproducer.

End of notes.
